verdict.rationale: Cerebras documents several latency-focused features: SDK TCP warming to reduce TTFT, payload compression that improves TTFT, streaming, a highest-priority service tier for time-critical user-facing requests, dedicated reserved capacity and predicted outputs. Independent hands-on reports consistently describe very high generation speed (e.g. breaking 300 tok/s, much faster than an 8x H100 setup, powering a voice assistant). One user reported hitting the per-minute request limit instantly, a caveat on sustained throughput rather than a contradiction of speed. Missing for 10: first-party quantified TTFT and tokens/sec benchmarks in the docs, and evidence that sustained high throughput holds under shared-tier rate limits.

support.subject: As a developer, I can serve latency-sensitive workloads with fast time-to-first-token and high-throughput generation

citations.quote: This SDK has a mechanism that sends a few requests to `/v1/tcp_warming` upon construction to reduce the TTFT.
This can meaningfully improve time-to-first-token (TTFT) for requests with long prompts.
Highest priority - requests are processed first. Use for time-critical, user-facing requests that require immediate processing.
Your endpoint runs on reserved capacity that is not shared with other customers, so your performance is never impacted by other workloads.
This is astonishingly fast. I'm struggling to get over 100 tok/s on my own Llama 3.1 70b implementation on an 8x H100 cluster.
